messages.author: 13b71855f1dab6f8
messages.subject: genome scan adjustment
parts:
Dear Karl, dear all,

in our study in mouse we are interested in genetic control of placenta weight from chromosome X. The belief that the genetic control is located on chromosome X is based on PREVIOUS studies of DIFFERENT authors. In our study ONLY chromosome X was genotyped.

Am I right to claim, that when computing significance threshold, it is necassary to adjust for a whole-genome scan which was (perhaps) performed by ohter authors many years ago? In practice, it means that
the X-chromosome specific false positive rate \alpha_X has to be modified the following way:

\alpha_X = 1-(1-\alpha)^{L_X/L} ,

where L is the genetic length of whole mouse genome amd L_X is genetic length of
chromosome X.

For adjusted p-value it holds:

p_X = 1-(1-p)^{L/L_X}.

In practice for L_X/L = 1/17 (in mouse) it means
\alpha_X=0.003 instead of unadjusted \alpha_X=0.05 and for example
instead of unadjusted p-value p=0.05 the adjusted one p_X=0.58.

Is it necassary to make such an adjustment?

I really appreciate your help.

Vaclav

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: genome scan adjustment
parts:
I would only adjust for the scan over the X chromosome. Adjust for the set of statistical tests that you're actually performing.

karl
